captions.text: Start in the Chicago Fire demonstration department.
Engine 51 and our officer personnel are fictional resources
for a training exercise.
Open Dispatch Settings and find Run Cards and Automatic Dispatch.
Select Closest Unit Response for this example, and leave automatic
dispatch off so a dispatcher can review the suggested resources.

spoken_references.Automatically dispatch recommended resou: dispatch off so a dispatcher can review

captions.text: Save, then reopen the page to confirm the choices.
A run card can override these department defaults, so check both
places when a result surprises you.

instruction_review.method: Actual JPEG review plus exact frozen speech/cue correspondence; literal controls preserved, contextual scene labels checked across intact screens. No inferred capture outcomes.

captions.text: Open Run Cards and choose a new card.
Name it Academy Training Alarm, and describe the exercise it supports.
In General, choose Pre-populate for dispatcher review.
Leave the card disabled while building it.
Home station supplies an origin when a call has no location;
required_labels: Home station (used when a call has no location)

spoken_references.Home station (used when a call has no lo: Home station supplies an origin when a call has no location

captions.text: it is not a substitute for checking an incident address.
Notice the other tabs: Triggers, Alarm Levels, Dispatchable
Statuses, and Test or Simulate.
Each controls a different part of the recommendation.

instruction_review.method: Actual JPEG review plus exact frozen speech/cue correspondence; literal controls preserved, contextual scene labels checked across intact screens. No inferred capture outcomes.

captions.text: On Triggers, choose Add Trigger and select Priority and Type.
Pick the department's training call type and an actual priority from the list.
This is more specific than matching either one alone.
On Alarm Levels, name level one Initial Response.
Add one Engine under Unit type requirements and one Officer
under Personnel role requirements.
Counts describe what the plan asks for; they do not create resources
or guarantee that a qualified, available person can be found.
Save this complete card while it remains disabled.

instruction_review.method: Actual JPEG review plus exact frozen speech/cue correspondence; literal controls preserved, contextual scene labels checked across intact screens. No inferred capture outcomes.

captions.text: Open Dispatchable Statuses before widening the plan.
An empty section follows the standard availability rules.
Selecting options replaces those rules for that section, so ticking only
one status can exclude the others.
To add Returning, begin with Start from the standard rules,
then add the appropriate meaning.
Prefer meanings when several custom labels share the same purpose.
A unit type can have its own rule, so inspect that section

spoken_references.By unit type: A unit type can have its own rule

captions.text: as well as All unit types.

instruction_review.method: Actual JPEG review plus exact frozen speech/cue correspondence; literal controls preserved, contextual scene labels checked across intact screens. No inferred capture outcomes.

captions.text: For a reusable response, open Response packages and create
Academy Initial Response.
Add a row that can pick one Engine and another that can pick one Officer.
Any of these allows alternative targets within a row.
Pick fills a count; Ensure first-arriving adds the earliest
matching resource only when another row has not already covered it.
Status narrows eligible resources.
Keep outstanding until sent preserves an unmet request for follow-up.
Save and reopen the package to verify the rows.

instruction_review.method: Actual JPEG review plus exact frozen speech/cue correspondence; literal controls preserved, contextual scene labels checked across intact screens. No inferred capture outcomes.

captions.text: Return to Alarm Levels and add a condition named Engine within eight minutes.
Choose Available within, Engine, a count of one, and 480 seconds.
Create two outcomes.
The Yes outcome sends Academy Initial Response; the No outcome
has no package and advises the dispatcher to review alternatives.

spoken_references.Advice for dispatchers: advises the dispatcher to review alternatives

captions.text: Mark the condition Start, then connect If yes and If no to the correct outcomes.
Every branch needs a destination.
Save the card before testing the decision you just changed.

instruction_review.method: Actual JPEG review plus exact frozen speech/cue correspondence; literal controls preserved, contextual scene labels checked across intact screens. No inferred capture outcomes.

scenes.title: Understand alternatives and fallbacks

captions.text: Arrives before compares one resource choice with another,
including turnout and travel time.
Use it when an earlier arrival changes the response you want.
Package rows can name a substitute package, and the card can relax status
filters for rows it cannot fill.
required_labels: Relax status filters for unfilled rows

spoken_references.Relax status filters for unfilled rows: filters for rows it cannot fill

captions.text: These choices can broaden a response, so document their purpose.
Missing or stale positions can make a decision uncertain.
Treat that warning as a reason to review available evidence, rather than as
proof that no suitable resource exists.
Watch the test with both fixed requirements and the same package: their
rows add together, so the card asks for another engine and reports a shortfall.
In this example we remove the fixed rows when moving to the conditional package.
The next test fills one engine and one officer without that duplication.

spoken_references.Engine 51: fills one engine and one officer
spoken_references.Personnel: fills one engine and one officer

visual_required_labels: Relax status filters for unfilled rows

instruction_review.method: Actual JPEG review plus exact frozen speech/cue correspondence; literal controls preserved, contextual scene labels checked across intact screens. No inferred capture outcomes.

captions.text: Open Test or Simulate.
Choose the priority, type, training coordinates, and
alarm level, then run the test.
Read the matched card and the path through its conditions.
Check the chosen outcome, recommended people and units,
and any shortfall or uncertainty.
This is a preview of current data, not a dispatched incident.
A saved card can be tested while disabled.
If you edit a rule, save it and run the test again so your
review matches the stored plan.
At the nearby training coordinates, Engine 51 meets the eight-minute
condition and the Initial Response package selects an engine and an officer.
At the farther test location, the No branch shows Review
alternatives with its advice.
These displayed times are estimates, not proof of a routed drive time.

instruction_review.method: Actual JPEG review plus exact frozen speech/cue correspondence; literal controls preserved, contextual scene labels checked across intact screens. No inferred capture outcomes.

scenes.title: Use the plan on Core New Call

captions.text: When testing is satisfactory, enable the card and open New Call.
Enter TRAINING ONLY in the name and nature, choose the matching type and
priority, and set the incident pin.
Wait for the Run Card panel and resource lists to refresh.
Review the actual decision, advice, selected resources,
and any response code choices.
The nearest list helps you inspect each suggestion.
You can change recipients before saving; a highlighted suggestion is still a
decision for the dispatcher to review.

instruction_review.method: Actual JPEG review plus exact frozen speech/cue correspondence; literal controls preserved, contextual scene labels checked across intact screens. No inferred capture outcomes.

scenes.title: Verify the result and maintain the card

captions.text: Save only inside your approved training environment, then open
the resulting call and confirm its recipients and alarm level.
A saved call does not establish that a member received an alert;
verify that separately through a controlled communication test.
Further alarm levels add requirements to an active response.
Review those levels before using Strike Next Alarm.
When starting from a gallery template, inspect its department mappings,
keep the created card disabled, and repeat the same saved-plan
test before putting it into use.

spoken_references.Run Test: test before putting it into use

captions.text: The same planning controls fit other organizations.
A community paramedicine or mental health team can request
a clinician and peer responder.
Search and rescue can request a search team and leader.
Security can combine a patrol unit with a site supervisor.
Wildland contractors can plan crew and support resources, while an
industrial team can request a response unit and a hazardous-materials role.
Configure the resource types, qualification checks and local
procedures for your own operation.
